title: Sirdar (Khartoum) to Herbert (Cairo), telegram ending in eight five-letter cipher groups
correspondents: Sirdar (Sir Reginald Wingate), Khartoum, to Herbert, Cairo
shelfmark: Durham University Library, Abbas Hilmi II papers, HIL/64/400 (digitised unit HIL/64/1-1011, frame 68 of 234, label 395-400, bottom right form)
folio_note: Egyptian State Telegraphs form G 14 (received), a clerk's copy. Original no. 408 (or 458), 57 words, 9-1-909, Khartoum to Herbert, Cairo, signed Sirdar. Clear English first: '74 I have received the following telegram begins the son of the late colonel Hassan bey Tewfik passed the medical examination and I beg you kindly to ask the Commandant to admit him to the Military school referring to your excellencies kind promise lady Bey Hassan Tewfiks ends', then 8 five-letter groups (40 letters), uncollated: Vdugk cesux ybypg eyybp xdwrt jbpef pzyot bpdjv (the hand writes b like a capital B; group 5 fourth letter r or e). No decode on the form.
status: 15 Nov 2026: cipher seen on the image (1,500-px IIIF region). All 546 frames of HIL/64 and HIL/65 looked at for a clear copy (same number, date, word count or wording): none found. Prior art not searched. HIL/66 onwards not opened.
why: A bare cipher passage, the Sirdar's own comment on a quoted request. The same file holds cipher/clear pairs of the same traffic and weeks (HIL/64/402 = 403, 3 Jan 1909; HIL/64/239-240 = 118-119, 30 Nov 1908; HIL/64/214 = 61-62, 26 Sept 1908), simple substitution regrouped in fives, so the alphabet can probably be rebuilt from them and applied.
score_note: 40 letters, too short alone; solvable if the Jan 1909 alphabet is the one of the nearby pairs (not tested).
verify: Collate the 8 groups from a full-resolution region; rebuild the alphabet from the 1908-09 pairs and test it; search the Sudan Archive (Wingate papers) for the telegram.

title: Siwa to the Director of the Coastguard, Alexandria: telegram with seven letter groups marked 'Secret ... code'
correspondents: Coastguard officer at Siwa (unsigned on the copy) to Director Sawahil (Coastguard Administration), Alexandria
shelfmark: Durham University Library, Abbas Hilmi II papers, HIL/65/273 and 272 (digitised unit HIL/65/1-1127, frame 63 of 312, label 272-277, top middle then top left)
folio_note: Egyptian State Telegraphs form G 13, a clerk's copy in two sheets. No. 3, 65 words, Siwa, 7.6.913, to Director Sawahil, Alexandria. '80. Boxes and effects for Sidi Ahmed have been delivered at Jaghboub stop following obtained by Aisa Mayrof and Bash Chawish Farag who went with same Secret ( aBmbd - xwlmh - bggtc - Fudug - v.t.li - medwd midibi - ) code Jaghboub to receive many notables expected from Egypt one of deserters Mansood Said is not dead but is at Nakhaila between Salloom and Derna'. Seven groups, uncollated, the last of six letters as written; dots stand for two letters of the fifth, with an Arabic word above it (perhaps 'mafqud', missing). No decode on the form.
status: 15 Nov 2026: cipher seen on the image (834-px IIIF region of the form). All 546 frames of HIL/64 and HIL/65 looked at for a clear copy (same number, date, station or wording): none found. Prior art not searched. HIL/66 onwards not opened.
why: Coastguard intelligence from the Senussi centre at Jaghbub with a short enciphered passage. The copyist's 'Secret ( ... ) code' may mark the Coastguard's own cipher or a code text obtained at Jaghbub; which is not settled. The 1912 Coastguard pair (HIL/64/890-891 = 737-739) gives a Coastguard alphabet to try.
score_note: About 36 letters with two lost; nature of the passage unsettled; only an older Coastguard alphabet to test.
verify: Collate from a full-resolution region; read the Arabic word over group 5; test the alphabet of HIL/64/890-891; look in HIL/66 onwards and in FO 141 / FO 371 for the Siwa report of 7 June 1913.

title: Malisudan (Khartoum) to Ferasudan (Cairo), telegram 672 with five five-letter cipher groups
correspondents: Malisudan (Sudan Government, Khartoum) to Ferasudan (Sudan Agency), Cairo
shelfmark: Durham University Library, Abbas Hilmi II papers, HIL/65/1122 (digitised unit HIL/65/1-1127, frame 310 of 312, label 1122-1123, left form)
folio_note: Egyptian State Telegraphs form G 13, a clerk's copy. No. 1796, words 42/44, Khartoum, 26 Feb 1914, to Ferasudan, Cairo, signed Malisudan. '672. Aglossa fss 69 over 28 fistularia no objection wftzk ccuqk knpby xpoyt xuota perhaps not necessary refer question to Dawa as this is continuation of examination but if Kabbud Cairo considers this necessary he may obtain authority direct.' Five five-letter groups (25 letters), uncollated (group 2 fourth letter q or g; group 3 second letter n or u), after two dictionary code words (Aglossa, fistularia). No decode on the form.
status: 15 Nov 2026: cipher seen on the image (1,900-px IIIF region). All 546 frames of HIL/64 and HIL/65 looked at for a clear copy or the telegram it answers: none found. Prior art not searched. HIL/66 onwards not opened.
why: A bare 25-letter passage in Sudan Government administrative traffic. The May 1913 pairs in the same file (HIL/65/157-158 = 159-160; HIL/65/148 = 153) are the nearest key material; whether that alphabet was still in use in Feb 1914 is not known.
score_note: 25 letters; depends wholly on an alphabet rebuilt from the 1913 pairs.
verify: Collate from a full-resolution region; rebuild the 1913 alphabet from the two pairs and test it; identify the code words from the Sudan Government code.
